lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Body Signals and Fueling My Day
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: noticing body signals

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 4 — body signals, rest, and food variety
objective: Learners identify and record four different body signals (hunger, thirst, tiredness, and needing a bathroom break) as each one shows up during one ordinary day, using neutral signal names instead of mood words, so they build a baseline noticing habit before naming or responding to signals in later lessons.
scenario: Across one regular day at home, the learner carries a small card divided into four boxes labeled hunger, thirst, tiredness, and bathroom need, and makes a tally mark in a box each time that signal shows up, without judging whether the timing was convenient.
materials: an index card or paper divided into four labeled boxes

tasks.directions: Before you start tallying, make a guess about today.

prompts.text: Guess which of the four signals (hunger, thirst, tiredness, bathroom need) you think you will notice the most times today, and explain why you picked it.

tasks.directions: Every time you notice one of the four signals today, make a tally mark in that box right away.

prompts.text: I made a tally mark within a few minutes of noticing the signal, not at the end of the day from memory.
I used one of the four neutral signal names (hungry, thirsty, tired, need a bathroom break) instead of a mood word like grumpy or bored.
I noticed and tallied at least three separate signal moments today.
I tallied a signal in the box that matched it, not in whichever box was closest.

tasks.directions: At the end of the day, add up the tally marks in each of the four boxes.

prompts.text: Which signal did you notice the most times today, and which did you notice the fewest times? Write both totals.

tasks.directions: Pick one specific tally mark from today and think back to that exact moment.

prompts.text: Describe one specific moment today when you noticed a signal and what you were doing right before you noticed it, such as playing outside, reading, or sitting still.

remediation: If a learner tallies boredom or restlessness as hunger, reteach with one distinguishing question before any tally is made: did the feeling start in the stomach, or did it start because you were waiting for something to do?
extension: Have the learner repeat the same four-box tally on a different kind of day and compare, in writing, which signal showed up in a different order between the two days.
